text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Crown Prince Hassan says every citizen is entitled to engage in dialogue and calls for exerting all efforts to gain right of compensation and right of return for Palestinian refugees.
- Palestinian Authority asks Jordan's land registry for land surveys in the West Bank.
- Livestock and Poultry lead the industrials in the Amman stock market, with prices and volume dropping after rebound.
- Crown Prince opens the industrial potash plant on Tuesday.
- Start of the parcel service between Jordan and Israel.
- Tenders announced for the internal infrastructure of Karak industrial city.
- Private sector allowed to import barley.
- (PM) Kabariti says seeks to expand the umbrella of the health insurance.
- Delegation of some of the authorities of the council of ministers to the finance and public works ministers.
- Smoking banned in public buses and the Amman Financial Market.
- Twenty-three donor and host country discuss on Monday solving the financial crisis of the UNRWA (United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in Near East).
- Islamic Action Front (IAF) party rejects joining cabinet, wants changes to election law.
